Subject: SparkVerse LlamaIndex + tracing integration — sandbox & rollout plan

Hi Priyanka — great to connect at KubeCon last month. Thanks for the follow-up.

High level: SparkVerse is looking to ship a new assistant that uses LlamaIndex on the client side and we'd like Redwood to provide a first-class integration (SDK connector + tracing hooks + canary fallback to a lower-cost model for certain routes).

Proposed scope (attached):
- LlamaIndex connector that can exchange embeddings and documents with Redwood endpoints; include sample mapping for metadata fields.
- Lightweight tracing integration (OpenTelemetry-compatible) that surfaces per-request latency + token-level cost to SparkVerse observability.
- Canary rollout plan: support for model fallback to a quantized variant when latency/cost thresholds exceeded.

Asks from SparkVerse:
1) A short technical kickoff (30–45m) to align API shapes and tracing expectations.
2) A staging window for a sandbox workspace that can run up to 8 concurrent sessions for two weeks.
3) Any security/compliance artifacts (SOC2 summary, data flow diagram) we should provide to procurement.

I've attached a first draft spec and a mutual action plan. Proposed times this week for a kickoff: Wed 11:00–12:00 PDT or Thu 14:00–15:00 PDT. If those don't work, send a couple of options and we'll accommodate.

Thanks — looking forward to shipping this with the SparkVerse team.

—

Hi Priyanka — Karthik from Redwood infra/serving runtime. Wanted to outline the tech approach so the kickoff is concrete:

1) Tracing & tagging
- We'll expose an OpenTelemetry-compatible span for each API request. You can attach request_id and customer_id as non-PII headers; we recommend hashing or tokenizing any customer identifier before sending it to the tracing span.
- Token-level cost attribution will be emitted as span attributes: tokens_input, tokens_output, token_cost_usd. These are numeric attributes you can join with your traces.

2) LlamaIndex connector notes
- The connector will call Redwood's /generate and /embed endpoints. We'll provide a lightweight client helper (Python) that maps LlamaIndex document metadata to Redwood's metadata fields and preserves provenance.
- We'll ship an example notebook and a test harness that runs against the sandbox workspace.

3) Canary + fallback
- We support policy-based routing. You can define per-route policies (latency threshold, cost-per-minute) that trigger fallback to a model alias (e.g., redwood-small-quant).
- Fallbacks are immediate and the runtime keeps per-route counters so you can set burst windows.

4) Security & data residency
- For the sandbox we'll provision an isolated tenant with logs retained for 90 days. For production we can propose a dedicated pool.

Questions for kickoff:
- For token-level cost showback, do you want raw token counts or pre-aggregated buckets (we can emit both)?
- Which LlamaIndex version do you plan to use in prod? We recommend v0.8+ for the connector.

Looking forward to Wed. I'll bring a short demo of the tracing spans.

—Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — that addresses most of our questions. A few procurement/contract items to surface ahead of kickoff:

- SLA: SparkVerse needs a written SLA for latency SLOs and an uptime target for the dedicated pool during our initial pilot (2 months). Can you share a sample SLA?
- Billing model: we'll need an expected cost estimate for a phased rollout (sandbox -> pilot -> production). Can Redwood provide a ballpark monthly run-rate for the pilot (we anticipate ~5M tokens/mo during pilot)?
- Security questionnaire: procurement has attached a 3rd-party intake — can Redwood assign a point of contact to fill it out (email to procurement@sparkverse.ai)?

I'll also note we prefer a canary that keeps a 90/10 split during first-week rollouts. Diego will add more detail on the integration requirements in the kickoff.
